name: Sagittarius A*
tagline: The Milky Way's supermassive black hole — four million suns in the dark.
history: At the galaxy's core, astronomers watched stars whip around an invisible point for three decades — the star S2 completes a full orbit in 16 years at up to 2.6% of light speed. Those orbits proved a mass of 4.3 million suns packed into a region smaller than the Solar System: a supermassive black hole, work that won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics. In May 2022 the Event Horizon Telescope — a virtual Earth-size array — released its actual image: a glowing ring of plasma around the shadow, only the second black hole ever photographed. Every large galaxy is now believed to host one, and this is ours.
source: Event Horizon Telescope; ESO; Nobel Prize 2020
